column1: pluralistic§A pluralistic reading list is harder to teach and worth the trouble.§**多元**的书单更难教，却值得费这个事。
poetic§Poetic licence does not cover getting the river's name wrong.§**诗的**自由不包括把河名写错。
poignant§Poignant is the word for a small loss, not a large one.§“**心酸**”这个词形容的是小的失去，而非大的。
polarization§Polarization of light through the crystal proved the theory.§光经晶体的**偏振**证实了这个理论。
polarize§The question polarizes a room that agrees on everything else.§这个问题让一个在别的事上都一致的房间**分裂**了。
polemic§A polemic persuades nobody and clarifies everything.§**论战**说服不了任何人，却让一切都清楚了。
politicize§Politicizing the appointment guaranteed a weaker candidate.§把这项任命**政治化**，注定会选出更弱的人选。
polymath§The last true polymath died before the journals multiplied.§最后一位真正的**博学者**死在期刊激增之前。
pomp§Pomp is expensive and, on the right day, worth it.§**排场**很花钱，在对的日子里却值得。
pompous§A pompous title on a modest paper does it no favours.§一篇朴实的论文配上**浮夸的**标题，只会害了它。
poorly§The photographs were poorly stored and half are gone.§这些照片**保存不善**，一半已经没了。
popularity§Popularity is a poor proxy for quality and an excellent one for reach.§**受欢迎程度**不能代表质量，却很能代表传播范围。
portent§He read every delay as a portent and was usually wrong.§他把每次延误都当作**预兆**，通常都错。
portray§She portrayed the queen for three seasons and never watched it.§她**演了三季女王**，却从没看过。
posthumous§Posthumous fame is of no use to anyone but the publisher.§**身后的名声**除了对出版商，对谁都没用。
potence§The potence of a dose is checked before every batch.§每批出货前都要检测剂量的**效力**。
potentate§A local potentate controlled the ferry and therefore the town.§一位**地方豪强**控制着渡口，因而控制着这个镇。
practicality§For all its practicality, the design was never built.§尽管很**实用**，这个设计从未被建造。
practitioner§Theory belongs to the reader; practice belongs to the practitioner.§理论属于读者，实践属于**从业者**。
pragmatic§Be pragmatic about the schedule and strict about the method.§在进度上**务实**，在方法上严格。
pragmatism§Pragmatism is a philosophy, not just an excuse.§**实用主义**是一种哲学，不只是借口。
pragmatist§The pragmatist won the argument and the idealist wrote the history.§**实用主义者**赢了争论，理想主义者写了历史。
praiseworthy§A praiseworthy failure deserves the same write-up as a success.§**值得称道**的失败应当得到与成功一样的记录。
prank§An elaborate prank in 1898 is still cited as evidence.§一八九八年一场精心策划的**恶作剧**至今仍被当作证据引用。
preachy§Nobody sets out to be preachy; it happens in the second draft.§没人一开始就想**说教**，那是在二稿里发生的。
precarious§The whole argument rests on a precarious assumption.§整个论证建立在一个**不稳固**的假设上。
precede§What precedes the crisis is usually more interesting than the crisis.§危机**之前**发生的事，通常比危机本身更有意思。
precipitate§Adding acid precipitates the salt out of solution.§加酸使盐从溶液中**沉淀**出来。
precipitous§A precipitous path down the cliff is the only way to the beach.§一条**陡峭的**崖径是通往海滩的唯一路径。
precise§Precise and accurate are not the same thing.§**精密**与准确不是一回事。
precision§Precision beyond what you can measure is decoration.§超出测量能力的**精确**只是装饰。
preclude§Being wrong once does not preclude being right later.§错过一次并不**妨碍**以后正确。
precocious§Precocious talent is often just early access.§**早熟的**才华往往只是更早的接触机会。
precursor§Symptoms appeared as a precursor two days before the storm.§风暴前两天就出现了作为**前兆**的迹象。
predetermine§Do not predetermine the answer by the way you ask.§不要用提问的方式预**先决**定答案。
predictable§Predictable is a compliment when it describes a train.§用来形容火车时，“**可预料**”是一句赞美。
prediction§A prediction with no date attached cannot be wrong.§不附日期的**预言**永远不会错。
predictive§Predictive text learns your habits and then enforces them.§**预测输入**学会你的习惯，然后强化它们。
predilection§His predilection for the minor key shaped the whole album.§他对小调的**偏爱**塑造了整张专辑。
predominant§The predominant view lasted until one careful count.§**主流**看法一直持续到一次仔细的清点。
preeminence§Preeminence in a small field is easily mistaken for greatness.§在一个小领域的**卓越**，很容易被误认为伟大。
preliminary§Preliminary results are the most quoted and least reliable.§**初步**结果被引用得最多，也最不可靠。
premature§A premature conclusion is harder to dislodge than no conclusion.§**过早的**结论比没有结论更难推翻。
prepossess§A prepossessing manner opened doors his work could not.§**讨人喜欢**的举止打开了他的作品打不开的门。
prescience§Prescience in a memo looks like luck in hindsight.§备忘录里的**先见**之明，事后看来像是运气。
prescient§Her prescient warning is quoted by people who ignored it.§她那份**有先见之明的**警告，被当初忽视它的人引用着。
prescribe§Do not prescribe a solution before you have named the problem.§在说清问题之前不要**开药方**。
prescriptive§A prescriptive rule about split infinitives has no basis.§关于分裂不定式的**规定**性规则毫无依据。
prestige§Prestige is what an institution spends when it has no money.§**声望**是机构没钱时花的东西。
prestigious§A prestigious journal rejected the paper that changed the field.§一份**声望很高的**期刊拒绝了那篇改变了整个领域的论文。
presumption§The presumption of innocence is a rule about evidence, not belief.§**无罪推定**是关于证据的规则，不是关于信念的。
presumptive§On presumptive evidence alone, they suspended the licence.§仅凭**推定**的证据，他们就吊销了执照。
presumptuous§It is presumptuous to speak for people who are in the room.§当事人就在场时替他们发言，未免**冒失**。
pretense§Under the pretense of a routine visit he checked the accounts.§他以例行拜访为**借口**查了账目。
pretentious§There is nothing pretentious about using the exact word.§用准确的词并不**做作**。
preternatural§The stillness before the storm was preternatural.§暴风雨前的静止**异乎寻常**。
pretext§Any pretext will do when the decision is already made.§决定既然已经作出，什么**借口**都行。
prevail§The southwesterly prevails here for nine months of the year.§这里一年有九个月**盛行**西南风。
prevalent§The spelling was prevalent until the first dictionary.§在第一部词典出现之前，这种拼法很**普遍**。
preventable§Most fires here are preventable and none are predicted.§这里大多数火灾都**可预防**，却没有一场被预测到。
preventive§A preventive check on Friday saves a Monday emergency.§周五的一次**预防**性检查，能省掉周一的紧急情况。
principal§The principal and the interest are listed separately.§**本金**与利息分别列出。
pristine§Nothing here is pristine; everything has been repaired twice.§这里没有什么是**原封未动**的，一切都修过两遍。
privacy§Privacy is not secrecy, though the two get confused.§**隐私**不是保密，尽管两者常被混淆。
proclaim§The roof proclaims the wealth the facade tries to hide.§屋顶**宣示**着立面试图掩藏的财富。
procurement§Procurement of the timber took longer than the carpentry.§**采购**木材比木工活花的时间还长。
prod§A prod in the ribs stopped him mid-sentence.§肋部被**戳了一下**，他话说到一半就停了。
